pencereler.0-5: Both engines died at under three thousand feet over New York. Just 208 seconds
pencereler.5-12: later, the jet was floating in the Hudson River. All 155 people aboard survived. The cause was a flock
pencereler.12-20: of Canada geese. The engines were tested against birds of about four pounds. Canada geese weigh about eight. Two engines, both beyond
pencereler.20-30: their design limit, at the same moment. The pilots' calm turned an engineering failure into a survival story.

segmentler.metin: US Airways Flight 1549 lost both engines and ditched in the Hudson.
It took only a flock of Canada geese.
So how could a flock of Canada geese do this?
The answer is dual-engine bird ingestion beyond the certification bird weight — and it is why bird-ingestion standards and airport wildlife control were reviewed after the ditching.
